name: Transit 4A Ablestar upper stage explosion
description: The first known on-orbit breakup: the Ablestar upper stage exploded hours after launch.

name: Pegasus HAPS upper stage explosion
description: The Pegasus HAPS stage from the STEP-2 launch exploded about two years after launch.

name: Fengyun-1C anti-satellite test
description: China destroyed its Fengyun-1C weather satellite with a ground-launched missile at about 865 km, creating the largest debris cloud on record.

name: USA-193 intercept (Operation Burnt Frost)
description: The US destroyed the failed USA-193 satellite at about 247 km; its debris re-entered within weeks.

name: Iridium 33 / Cosmos 2251 collision (Cosmos 2251 fragments)
description: The first accidental hypervelocity collision between two intact satellites, at about 789 km over Siberia.

name: Iridium 33 / Cosmos 2251 collision (Iridium 33 fragments)
description: The first accidental hypervelocity collision between two intact satellites, at about 789 km over Siberia.

name: Mission Shakti anti-satellite test
description: India destroyed its Microsat-R satellite at about 283 km; most fragments re-entered within a few years.

name: Kosmos 1408 anti-satellite test
description: Russia destroyed the defunct Kosmos 1408 satellite with a direct-ascent missile at about 480 km.

name: Long March 6A upper stage breakup
description: The upper stage from a Yunhai-3 launch broke up in orbit shortly after launch.

name: Long March 6A upper stage breakup
description: The upper stage that launched the first Qianfan (Thousand Sails) satellites broke up in orbit.
